newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's Cardoso urges progress on reforms.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's Cardoso urges progress on reforms.

text.p: Brazilian President Fernando Henrique Cardoso Friday urged Congress to speed on with approval of key fiscal reforms and said he hoped civil service and pension reforms will be voted on by June, his spokesman said.
Spokesman Sergio Amaral said Cardoso also accepted that a "slight exception to the salary ceiling might be the price we have to pay" for approval of civil service reform.

"The president said that the reforms in general have advanced...and that he hoped they would be fully approved, in both houses of Congress, by June, that is in the first half of 1997," Amaral told reporters after a minsterial cabinet meeting.
Reforms of the pension system are in the Senate where the government hopes to rewrite a bill heavily watered down by the Chamber of Deputies.
The civil service reform was due to have been voted on in the lower house last Wednesday, but the ballot was postponed until next week.
The government conceded at the last moment to an increase in a proposed 10,800 real a month ceiling for public sector salaries.
